Bone marrow aspirate ⍉needed unless atypical sx (constitutional sx or organomegaly)
- most resolve w.in 3–6mo of sx onset regardless of tx
- cutaneous bleed only → outpt; ⍉bleed or mild cutaneous only → observation
- chronic ITP: TPO receptor agonists (eltrombopag, romiplostim) = preferred steroid-sparing 2nd-line
Tx by bleed severity + degree of thrombocytopenia:
- life-threatening bleed: PLT transfusion, glucocorticoids (ex, methylprednisolone), IVIG, + anti-D immune globulin (Rh⊕ pts) ± romiplostim (TPO receptor agonist); refractory → splenectomy
- severe, non-life-threatening bleed: ED eval + hospital admit; combo glucocorticoids, IVIG, or anti-D ± romiplostim
- mod/high bleed risk: rapid plt rise needed (ex, procedure w/ expected blood loss, head trauma w/o ICH) → IVIG; ⍉rapid rise needed → PO glucocorticoids (ex, dexamethasone or prednisone)
All pts: restrict activity, ⍉antiplatelet drugs + anticoagulants, regular monitoring; menstruating adolescents may need hormonal tx (prevent menorrhagia)
